gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Editorial swagger with a soft felt-marker swell: Quilon thickens and thins just enough to feel inked by hand. And Noto Sans Coptic keeps its middle zone dominant, with uncrowded mouths that let extended text glide along.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Editorial through and through, Quilon carries a modest, readable shift in weight across every curve of its letters. Noto Sans Cuneiform has swollen glass-bead lowercase, so give it modest size.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Soft and confident: Quilon steps gently from heavy to light, while Noto Sans Devanagari keeps a compact skyline. Quilon grabs attention; the sans-serif body does the quiet explaining.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Contemporary through and through, Quilon swells in measured steps from hairline to stem. And Noto Sans Elbasan has large lowercase and open terminals, so it can be sized down without pinching.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Sharp but unfussy: Quilon lightens its diagonals just slightly against the verticals, giving headings a quiet editorial polish. Then Noto Sans Elymaic delivers the clarity, its open apertures keeping every letter easy to tell apart.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Quilon carries the mild thick-thin variation of a letterpress slug, which gives its headings an editorial, inked authority. And Noto Sans Ethiopic, sturdy and open at the c terminals, carries paragraphs without a snag.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Noto Sans Georgian reads cleanly, with curves that stay open throughout the alphabet and ascender stems kept short. Quilon makes the entrance; the sans quietly does the carrying.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Crisp and inked: Quilon draws moderate thick-thin strokes, while Noto Sans Grantha presses its bowls flat like pen nibs. Quilon does its best work as a large, confident title.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi leans on crayon-heavy lowercase strokes and generous terminal gaps, beneath Quilon, whose contrast stays medium without sharp hairlines. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi then carries paragraphs with easy, sturdy momentum.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aram: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads friendly, its c ends opening like pincers. Quilon, steady yet faintly modulated in its line, does its finest work at display sizes where its commanding presence can show.
